references.text: Here the sons of Israel are mentioned again in connection with their arrival in Egypt, reflecting their significance as the tribes of Israel.
Moses blesses the tribes of Israel before his death, parallel to Jacob's blessings of his sons.
The list of Jacob's sons, which forms the basis for the twelve tribes.
By faith Jacob blessed each of Joseph's sons, referring to the blessings in Genesis 49.
The blessing of the tribes (Gen 49) is linked to the historical fulfillment of the land promise in Joshua.
The identity of the twelve tribes established in Genesis carries forward the high priest's service in Exodus.
The blessing of the twelve tribes in Genesis finds liturgical expression in the high priest's breastpiece.
The identity of the twelve tribes in Genesis forms the basis for the land distribution in Ezekiel's prophecy.
The blessing of the tribes in Genesis leads forward to their gathering for worship in the book of Psalms.
